why: Shorter, neutral, three plain questions plus a concrete next action; B recites a four-risk framework in bullets.
Author's own rough first-person voice, used sparingly, gives the story and why the closing line lands.
Guess comes before the answer is revealed, so the prediction exercise works and the slide has fewer sentences.
Drops the extra 'shape the rules together' sentence; fewer words, same point.
Cuts the trailing sentence that is a vague closer ('possible problem'); shorter and cleaner.
'Run' is a concrete picturable word, while 'session' is the author's rejected wording in the same line; A also keeps the patronizing 'nobody can hand you' either way, so go with the wording fix.
Title carries the concept as a claim rather than the abstract 'The generalisation'; the closing line is shorter.
Cuts the parenthetical callback to M6, which is a pre-read abstraction, and the flywheel closer; fewer words.
Cuts the restating tail 'shape the whole map has had from the start'; fewer words.
Cuts the moralising closer 'the one that counts'.
'Prompts' names what was actually run and is more precise than 'exercise'; the rest is identical.
Fewer words; B's added clauses restate what is already said.
Drops the forward hint to Module 4 and the vague 'that list is the lesson'; shorter and concrete.
'The training runs on YOUR real work' is a neutral statement; A's 'is the material' is odder phrasing.
Cuts the restating sentence opener; fewer words.
Cuts the forward-hint closer about Phases 3 and 4.
Fewer words; the extra sentence in B restates what the agent does and is not needed.
'It often isn't. It's a draft' is the smoother rhythm and keeps the deliberate parallel; B's 'just' adds a diminishing tone.
B's extra sentence is a meta aside ('you are not learning them here') that adds words and no action.
Shorter and plain; A adds a trainer-performance cue ('watch rather than type along') that makes the student passive.
'Three' is a count the reader would have to check; 'new concerns' is neutral and shorter.
'Three pressures' gives the slide a clear count and structure that matches the three bullets.
'Where the file gets read' is a plain, picturable title; 'Three agents using the file' is vaguer.
Fewer words; B adds MCP-connector detail that is a tool feature the agent can explain on request.
Cuts the closing restatement ('Three modules in, this is your practice now'), which is fewer words and a declared narrator line.
Terser, reads faster and more neutral; B adds many words and the clause-heavy detail.
Drops the redundant 'This is your side-quest lane' line, since fewer words are better.
Cuts the extra opening sentence and its hedge, which gives fewer words with the same content.
'Check' is the author's wanted verb, and 'Read' implies reading all of it; 'spot-check' fits better still.
A is shorter and picturable ('forest before the trees'); B is a more abstract claim.
The title 'A check resets the chain' states the action and is shorter.
Instruction title gives a concrete action to take instead of a statement that puts the LLM first.
Matches the author's call: gives the recommended, just-now-possible option and tells them to ask Claude.
A is shorter, while B adds 'written as an ADR' with more words for little gain.
The author rejected 'the wall' as a made-up concept; A drops it.
A concrete, picturable title; A's title is a longer abstract claim.
Shorter header; 'window' alone is the picturable term and matches the author's brevity preference.
Cuts the extra closing remark; fewer sentences, no restating hedge.
'Things a good plan has' avoids a count that must match the list and is fewer words.
Gives the student a concrete action in their own control instead of a bare imperative with no object.
Cuts the closing restatement sentence; fewer sentences per slide.
Permission framing that lands twice with its why, which the author explicitly values.
A concrete action the student can take, short and active; A is abstract and puts the student in a passive 'consume' frame.
Drops the extra orientation sentences; fewer words and no forward-hint closers.
'Alternative' is plain and picturable, and the cut removes an unneeded giving-the-floor clause; fewer words.
